tasks.short: Chair department meetings and decide department matters, handle leave, travel and budget requests, prepare department figures, and answer administrative e-mail.

steps.what: Lecturer chairs department meetings and decides department matters as department head
Lecturer handles leave, travel and budget requests by e-mail
Lecturer prepares department figures on staffing, teaching load and budget in spreadsheets
Lecturer answers administrative e-mail from staff and the dean's office

tasks.design: Leave, travel and budget requests arrive as workflow items in the HR and expense systems ({HCM}, {EXPENSE}) with the remaining leave or budget shown, so the head decides in one screen instead of checking figures by e-mail. A department dashboard ({BI}) shows staffing, teaching load and budget use from the source systems. Chairing meetings, deciding and answering e-mail stay with the head.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by e-mail without figures, and department figures were built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: HR and expense systems route requests with balances; dashboards read source systems.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching load data sit in separate tools.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a dispute between colleagues fairly.
tasks.altitude: The head decides instead of compiling figures.

evidence.claim: HR and expense systems route requests with balances; dashboards read source systems.
Dashboards that show figures per staff member can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the department agenda to e-mail answered; faculty-level decisions are outside.
Input contract: request workflows set up; fallback is e-mail.
Staff file requests in the system in about the time an e-mail took.

incremental.description: Lecturer chases requests stuck in the workflow.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small departments; high: large departments with many requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write job postings, screen applications, interview candidates, train new writing instructors, and supervise them through class visits.

steps.what: Lecturer writes job postings to recruit department personnel
Lecturer screens applications from e-mail attachments
Lecturer trains new faculty and student writing instructors
Lecturer supervises instructors through class visits

tasks.design: Job postings start from the department's earlier postings stored as templates in the recruitment system ({ATS}). Applications arrive there with all documents per candidate in one place, so the lecturer does not sort e-mail attachments; no software ranks candidates. Interviewing, training and supervising stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Postings were written from scratch and applications sorted from e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitment systems hold posting templates and application files.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a candidate can explain writing to a nervous student.

evidence.claim: Recruitment systems hold posting templates and application files per candidate.
AI used for recruitment or selection is high-risk; here no software ranks candidates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vacancy to instructors supervised; contracts are outside.
Input contract: vacancies run through the recruitment system; fallback is e-mail.
Candidates apply online in about the time an e-mail took.
research_questions: Is screening time per vacancy shorter?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few vacancies; high: many student instructor hires.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the student's draft, point out citation and format errors, discuss structure and argument, and book sessions and keep session records.

steps.what: Lecturer reads the student's draft in the writing center
Lecturer points out citation and format errors to students
Lecturer provides assistance on structure and argument
Lecturer books sessions by e-mail and keeps session records on paper

tasks.design: Before a session, students run their draft through the formative feedback tool in the learning system ({LMS}), which comments on citation style and set format criteria, so sessions spend little time on these. Students book a slot online with a short intake form, and a session record template replaces paper notes. Reading the draft and helping with structure and argument stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions spent time on format errors, and bookings and records were handled by e-mail and paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems give formative feedback; booking tools take intake forms.
tasks.still_hard: Walk-in students skip the feedback tool.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student who has given up on an essay start again.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer spends sessions on ideas.

evidence.claim: FeedbackFruits Automated Feedback gives formative feedback on writing criteria such as citation style; teachers edit the criteria.
Student data processing needs a legal basis and minimal data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session booked to the session recorded; grading is outside.
Input contract: feedback tool licensed; fallback is pointing errors out in session.
Students spend a little time on the feedback tool and booking; priced as customer time.
Help on argument does not change.
research_questions: Do sessions cover more argument and less format?

incremental.description: Lecturer sets feedback criteria for common assignment types.
Students run drafts through the feedback tool and book online.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many walk-ins; high: booked sessions with feedback run first.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather teaching evaluations, publications and teaching load, hold the evaluation meeting, write the report, check it with the staff member's comments, and submit it to HR.

steps.what: Lecturer gathers teaching evaluations, publications and teaching load from several systems
Lecturer conducts the staff performance evaluation meeting
Lecturer completes the report form, which fills in teaching load, course evaluation scores and publications
Lecturer writes the judgement on the staff member's performance in the report
Lecturer checks the final report with the staff member's comments
Lecturer e-mails the signed report to HR

tasks.design: An evaluation view in the HR system ({HCM}) brings together the staff member's teaching load, course evaluation scores and publication list from their source systems, so the head does not gather them from several screens. The report form fills those facts in; the head writes the judgement, and no software proposes ratings. Once the head has checked the report with the staff member's comments, it is signed and stored in the HR system instead of e-mailed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts were gathered from several systems and the report typed in full.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems combine data from source systems into evaluation forms.
tasks.still_hard: Course evaluation scores need context to be fair.
tasks.human_edge: Giving a colleague honest feedback they can act on.
tasks.altitude: The head judges instead of collecting facts.

evidence.claim: HR systems can combine data from source systems into evaluation forms.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the evaluation due to the report submitted; pay decisions are outside.
Input contract: works council consent for the evaluation view; fallback is gathering by hand.
The judgement stays with the head; no ratings are proposed.
Staff members' time does not change.
research_questions: Is preparation time per evaluation shorter?

incremental.description: Lecturer corrects wrong facts in the evaluation view.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the head with the staff member's comments in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few evaluations; high: large departments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The lecturer as head keeps deciding, interviewing, training, helping students and judging colleagues; e-mail requests, figure compiling, format corrections and fact gathering shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A head with more time for people.

job.title: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
